traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 237 Rubiaceae (order Rubiales): trees and shrubs, less often herbs; leaves opposite or in whorls, simple, mostly entire; stipules between or within the leaf stalks, sometimes as leafy as the leaves; flowers mostly regular, rarely slightly irregular; corolla sitting on the ovary, more or less a tube, with 4 to 10 lobes and as many stamens; ovary inferior; fruit a capsule, berry or drupe. The corolla's funnel shape in some is read from 'more or less tubular'. Library 1.0's Rubiaceae are 72% shrubs and trees.

traits.zygomorphy.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Rubiaceae with Dialypetalanthaceae, Henriqueziaceae, Naucleaceae, Theligonaceae: its irregular flowers are of no named kind (pea flower, two lips, orchid lip), read from the coded corolla symmetry (spec-rework/b1/delta): zygomorphy other. Its flowers are not mostly zygomorphic, so a plant of it states its own symmetry; one that is zygomorphic draws this kind, and one stating none is drawn regular.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 409, 411, 412, family Rubiaceae: phyllotaxis pattern decussate, often; read as {"decussate": "often"}.

traits.inflorescence.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 409, 411, 412, family Rubiaceae: inflorescence cyme, rarely solitary, usually; read as {"cyme": "usually", "solitary": "rarely"}.

traits.sexual_system.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 409, 411, 412, family Rubiaceae: sexual system hermaphrodite, usually; read as {"hermaphrodite": "usually"}.
